key_highlights: ASX closed the week lower as traders priced in higher RBA rates, with hyperscaler bond issuance globally pushing yields up (#5, #58)
Iron ore market facing a structural shakeout masked by geopolitical conflict, pressuring BHP, RIO, FMG (#60)
Bathla collapse signals broader construction sector stress; housing construction expected to follow prices lower (#54, #59, #61)
EV sales surpassed petrol cars in Australia for first time; BYD confirms EV tipping point reached (#35, #51)
Qantas operational disruption (engine fire, flight diversion) raises safety and cost concerns for QAN.AX (#18, #43)
ASIC launched whistleblower review at Big 4 accounting firms, adding regulatory overhang to financials (#62)
CBA and Westpac flagged for charging loyal customers more via legal loophole, reputational risk (#68)
Aurum Resources added high-grade gold ounces in West Africa; small-cap miners (Kaoko, Vanadium, Piche) led ASX runners (#48, #49, #50)
El Nino spawning cyclone triplets threatens Qld assets and insurance sector (#56)
Australia's per-capita economy stalling while Canada's soars, raising structural competitiveness concerns (#65)

sectors.trend: Iron ore shakeout underway amid geopolitical distraction; gold miners showing relative strength. Small-cap explorers (Kaoko, Vanadium, Piche, Brightstar, Solstice, Power Minerals) outperforming on capital raises and discovery news.
sectors.implications: BHP.AX, RIO.AX, FMG.AX face margin pressure from iron ore price softness. Gold names (GOLD.AX, NVG.AX, AUC.AX) benefit from safe-haven flows. Small-caps volatile but offer asymmetric upside.

sectors.trend: Regulatory and reputational overhang: ASIC whistleblower review at Big 4 accountants; CBA and Westpac flagged for discriminatory pricing. Victoria's soaring debt raises sovereign credit concerns.
sectors.implications: CBA.AX, WBC.AX, NAB.AX, ANZ.AX face potential NCCP/ASIC scrutiny. Higher rates support NIM but cap rate cycle limits upside. Defensive positioning warranted.

sectors.trend: EV adoption crossed tipping point in Australia; fuel margins surging globally (Murphy USA). VW cutting 50,000 jobs signals auto sector distress. BYD dominance accelerating.
sectors.implications: WES.AX, AGL.AX, SGP.AX benefit from EV charging demand. Oil & gas (WDS.AX, WES.AX) face structural demand risk. Consumer staples (WOW.AX, WES.AX) resilient.

sectors.trend: Bathla collapse exposes construction sector fragility; housing construction to follow prices lower. Brisbane waterfront approved but zero affordable units. El Nino cyclone risk to Qld assets.
sectors.implications: REITs (GPW.AX, ICPS.AX, DGL.AX) face occupancy and construction cost risks. Construction names (WBC.AX exposure, CSL.AX unaffected) under pressure. Insurance (WBC.AX, CGU.AX) faces cyclone claims.

sectors.trend: Vietnam dental tourism threatens Australian dental practices. AI worker shortage flagged by Pocock. Broadcom AI revenue soaring but Wall Street wants more.
sectors.implications: CSL.AX, SGH.AX, HIC.AX face competitive pressure from offshore medical tourism. Tech exposure via global AI capex cycle remains positive but valuation-stretched.

sectors.trend: Qantas engine fire and flight diversion raise safety and operational cost concerns. Defence sector disrupted by cheap drone technology.
sectors.implications: QAN.AX faces reputational and cost headwinds. ASX defence names (STO.AX, WES.AX adjacent) see margin compression from drone competition.

market_outlook.short_term: ASX likely to remain under pressure in the 1–3 month window. Rate fears from global bond supply and RBA constraints cap upside. Iron ore softness and construction stress weigh on materials and industrials. Geopolitical headlines (Russia, US-Iran) create volatility. 'Bull case returns' narrative (#63) offers counterpoint but unconfirmed. Expect range-bound trading with downside bias.
market_outlook.long_term: 6–12 month outlook cautiously constructive if RBA eases and iron ore stabilises. EV adoption, gold, and small-cap discovery themes offer structural upside. However, Australia's stalling per-capita growth vs Canada (#65) and construction sector fragility cap the bull case. Housing construction following prices lower is a multi-year headwind for REITs and builders.
